title: Scripture of a rite, pattern Mark II
description: A rite brings the machine into one of its aspects, or, written as an edict, is proclaimed whole and bears no aspect at all; it is kept in the rites/ hall of the Librarium and bears the name of its scripture. A rite of aspects declares the subjects it reads and sets and the observances it speaks when they change; an edict keeps a liturgy in the designation form. Scripture of pattern Mark I is converted by the servitor on its first reading, and is judged by no schema. Only the form of each key is judged here; recite 'servitor inquisition' for the full judgement of the Inquisition, and 'servitor expound <key>' for the lore of any key.

edict.description: Only "edict": true makes the rite an edict; false is as if unwritten.

inscriptions.description: The inscriptions of an edict, each decreeing at most one plain word.

decrees.description: The one word an edict inscribes when the invocation gives none; an edict bears no aspect, so it holds no aspect map.

inscriptions.description: The inscriptions of a rite of aspects, whose decrees are always an aspect map.

decrees.description: The word each aspect inscribes when the invocation gives none: always an aspect map, {"*": "<word>"} for one word for every aspect; it may leave aspects without decree.

pattern.description: The Mark of the form in which this scripture is written: "Mark II".

purpose.description: The words that tell a reader why the rite exists, shown by the census and the cogitator. Never illuminated.

aspects.description: The named conditions the rite can bring the machine into, written by hand: at least one, each named once. An edict bears none.

edict.description: Marks the rite an edict when true: a rite without aspects, proclaimed whole each time it is invoked, whose liturgy holds incantations and litanies in the designation form, every word written once. False is as if unwritten.

inscriptions.description: Named words carried by one invocation, spoken as the rune --<key>, illuminated as {{inscription.<key>}} and kept on the data-slate. Each key names one inscription.

not.description: The runes the servitor bears for its own rituals, which no inscription may take as its name.

tongue.description: The program in which this rite's words are spoken, unless a subject, observance or entry names its own; the settings' tongue, else bash, when unwritten.

vox-cast.description: The tidings the rite sends of its invocation: "progress" tells of each subject that changed, or of each verse of an edict, and "success" proclaims triumph. Each at most once, in any order; tidings of a fall are proclaimed unbidden.

subjects.description: What a rite of aspects reads and sets, in written order: at least one subject, each named once and shaped by its designation.

observances.description: The named deeds of a rite of aspects, spoken once when a subject that names them changes: before the first such subject as its introit, or after the last as its recessional.

liturgy.description: The liturgy of an edict: incantations and litanies in the designation form, performed one after another as written, each named by its verse.

$schema.description: The schema this scripture is written against, for the editors of the faithful. The servitor accepts it and heeds it not.

name.description: A name fit for an aspect or an inscription: a letter or digit, then only letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'.

aspectKey.description: A key of an aspect map: a declared aspect, or "*" to serve every aspect not named.

word.description: Words that may not be empty, for the servitor cannot perform what names nothing.

command.description: Words that may not be empty, in which placeholders such as {{aspect}} are filled at invocation.

patience.description: How long a command may labour before it is deemed to have fallen: a span greater than nothing, such as "500ms", "5s" or "2m".

inscription.description: One inscription of the rite: why it exists, whether an invocation may proceed without it, and the word each aspect decrees when the invocation gives none.

purpose.description: The words that tell a reader why the inscription exists, shown beside its rune.

mandatory.description: Whether an invocation must carry this inscription, by its rune or by a decree; an invocation without it then falls in the pre-flight.

decrees.description: The word each aspect inscribes when the invocation gives none: one word for every aspect, or an aspect map that may leave aspects without decree.

tome.description: Scripture drawn from another scripture-file rather than written inline, read anew in every pre-flight.
The path of the tome; a path that does not begin at the root is reckoned from the hall of the rite's scripture.

illuminate.description: Whether the placeholders within the tome are filled; else its scripture is placed verbatim.

scripture.description: What a sanctum or transcription places into its vessel: inline words, a list of lines joined as one, or a tome.

zeal.description: Leave for a transcription or tether subject to overwrite what the servitor did not itself create.

exalted.description: Whether the subject, observance or verse is set or spoken not with its invoker's authority but with the machine's own, by an exalted servitor from the sanction its master gave: true for every aspect or for none, never an aspect map. Its words are fixed at the sanction, so {{former}} and an inscription only its rune may fill are heresy within them; an exalted vessel or bound name begins at the root once rendered and lies not beneath /proc, /sys or /dev. False is as if unwritten.

relics.description: The scriptures exalted speech reads beside its scroll, each named by its place within the hall of the rite's scripture; their words are sealed into the sanction, and the exalted servitor lays them under the same names in a hall of its own. Only an exalted step bears relics.

items.description: One relic: a path within the hall of the rite, never beginning at the root.

omenMap.description: A map keyed by aspect, always an object, with "*" serving every aspect it does not name; pattern Mark II knows no single value in its stead.

byOmen.description: Words keyed by the omens a machine-spirit declares, always an object, with "*" serving every omen it does not name.

plain.description: Words written once for every aspect, never an aspect map; they may be empty.

guard.description: Declared aspects that admit an observance; every aspect when unwritten.

references.description: The names of observances declared under "observances".

subject.description: One subject of a rite of aspects, shaped by its "designation": a sanctum, a transcription, a tether or a machine-spirit.

subject-sanctum.description: A subject that keeps a warded region of a vessel, read by the aspect its marker records and set by rewriting the region and its marker.

name.description: The name of the subject, unique within the rite.

purpose.description: Words that tell a reader why the subject exists. Never illuminated.

omens.description: The scripture the sanctum keeps for each aspect; never null, "" keeps it empty.

exalted.description: Whether the subject is set with the machine's own authority, from a sanction; its vessel then begins at the root.

introit.description: The observances spoken before the subject changes.

recessional.description: The observances spoken after the subject changed.

vessel.description: The vessel the sanctum is kept in. A leading "~" and $NAMES are expanded.

ward.description: The name that marks this sanctum within its vessel; the rite's name when unwritten. No whitespace.

glyph.description: The mark that opens the sanctum's markers in the vessel's own tongue; divined from the vessel's name when unwritten.

closing-glyph.description: The mark that seals the sanctum's markers where remarks must be closed; divined with the glyph when unwritten.

consecrate.description: Leave to bring the vessel into being should it be missing.

subject-transcription.description: A subject that is a whole vessel, read by comparing its scripture with each aspect's omen and set by writing it anew or striking it.

name.description: The name of the subject, unique within the rite.

purpose.description: Words that tell a reader why the subject exists. Never illuminated.

omens.description: The scripture of the vessel for each aspect, or null where the vessel shall not be.

exalted.description: Whether the subject is set with the machine's own authority, from a sanction; its vessel then begins at the root.

introit.description: The observances spoken before the subject changes.

recessional.description: The observances spoken after the subject changed.

vessel.description: The vessel written anew. A leading "~" and $NAMES are expanded.

seal.description: The rights of reading, writing and execution the vessel is to bear, as three or four octal numerals.

zeal.description: Leave to overwrite what the servitor did not itself create.

force.description: The same leave as "zeal" under another name; write "zeal", never both.

subject-tether.description: A subject that is a bound name, read by comparing where it leads with each aspect's omen and set by binding, rebinding or unbinding it.

name.description: The name of the subject, unique within the rite.

purpose.description: Words that tell a reader why the subject exists. Never illuminated.

omens.description: Where the tether leads for each aspect, or null where it shall be unbound.

exalted.description: Whether the subject is set with the machine's own authority, from a sanction; its bound name then begins at the root.

introit.description: The observances spoken before the subject changes.

recessional.description: The observances spoken after the subject changed.

tether.description: The name bound. A leading "~" and $NAMES are expanded.

zeal.description: Leave to overwrite what the servitor did not itself create.

force.description: The same leave as "zeal" under another name; write "zeal", never both.

subject-machine-spirit.description: A subject read by its auspex and set by its enact words: one omen for each aspect, the aspect's own name when "omens" is unwritten.

name.description: The name of the subject, unique within the rite.

purpose.description: Words that tell a reader why the subject exists. Never illuminated.

omens.description: The omen of each aspect: the words its auspex shows when the machine stands in that aspect.

exalted.description: Whether the enact words are spoken with the machine's own authority, from a sanction.

introit.description: The observances spoken before the subject changes.

recessional.description: The observances spoken after the subject changed.

auspex.description: How the machine-spirit is read; without one it is enacted on every invocation and never proven.

enact.description: The words that set the machine-spirit into each omen, which they hear as {{omen}} and SERVITOR_OMEN.

tongue.description: The program in which its words are spoken; the rite's tongue when unwritten.

patience.description: How long its enact words may labour before they are slain and deemed fallen.

relics.description: The scriptures its exalted words read beside them.

allOf.description: Relics are borne only by an exalted subject.

exalted.description: A subject bearing relics must be exalted.

allOf.description: An exalted auspex reads only an exalted subject.

exalted.description: The subject of an exalted auspex must be exalted.

spiritAuspex.description: The auspex of a machine-spirit: its scan, its trials, or both.

scan.description: Words, spoken once, whose output is the omen the subject shows.

trials.description: One trial per omen, a death-mark of 0 telling that the subject shows it; an omen without a trial is what remains when every trial fails.

patience.description: How long the auspex may labour before the subject is deemed mute.

exalted.description: Whether the auspex is spoken by the exalted servitor at invocation alone, for a subject only the machine's own authority can read.

observance.description: One named deed of a rite of aspects, shaped by its "designation": an incantation or a litany.

observance-incantation.description: An observance that speaks one line of words.

name.description: The name of the observance, unique within the rite.

to.description: The aspects the observance is spoken into.

from.description: The aspects the observance is spoken out of.

words.description: The words spoken, once for every aspect.

tongue.description: The program in which the words are spoken.

patience.description: How long the words may labour before they are slain and deemed fallen.

reversion.description: The words that undo the observance should the invocation fall.

exalted.description: Whether the words are spoken with the machine's own authority, from a sanction.

relics.description: The scriptures the exalted words read beside them.

observance-litany.description: An observance that recites a whole written scroll of commands.

name.description: The name of the observance, unique within the rite.

to.description: The aspects the observance is spoken into.

from.description: The aspects the observance is spoken out of.

scroll.description: The path of the scroll, once for every aspect.

offerings.description: What is laid before the scroll, each word written once.

tongue.description: The program through which a scroll the machine may not execute is recited.

patience.description: How long the litany may labour before it is slain and deemed fallen.

reversion.description: The words that undo the observance should the invocation fall.

exalted.description: Whether the scroll is recited with the machine's own authority, from a sanction.

relics.description: The scriptures the scroll of the exalted litany reads beside it.

entry.description: One entry of an edict's liturgy, shaped by its "designation": an incantation or a litany, named by its verse.

entry-incantation.description: An entry of an edict that speaks one line of words.

tongue.description: The program in which the words are spoken.

patience.description: How long the words may labour before they are slain and deemed fallen.

reversion.description: The words that undo this entry should the proclaiming fall.

exalted.description: Whether the words are spoken with the machine's own authority, from a sanction.

relics.description: The scriptures the exalted words read beside them.

entry-litany.description: An entry of an edict that recites a whole written scroll of commands.

scroll.description: The path of the scroll, written once.

offerings.description: What is laid before the scroll, each word written once.

tongue.description: The program through which a scroll the machine may not execute is recited.

patience.description: How long the litany may labour before it is slain and deemed fallen.

reversion.description: The words that undo this entry should the proclaiming fall.

exalted.description: Whether the scroll is recited with the machine's own authority, from a sanction.

relics.description: The scriptures the scroll of the exalted litany reads beside it.

exaltedRelics.description: Relics are borne only by exalted speech.

exalted.description: Speech bearing relics must be exalted.
